$comment: Record classes this SDK registers that spec's own record-bearing rule does not yet reach. A GATE INPUT, not a filter: scripts/build-record-types.mjs adds these to the derived population, and tests/record-types/derivation.test.ts fails when an entry no longer needs to be here. So the list can only shrink, and shrinking it is an explicit committed edit.
$rule: scripts/check-class-coverage.py in the spec repository defines the population: a class whose rdfs:subClassOf chain reaches prov:Entity or prov:Activity has said its instances are record data. It is the only machine-readable statement anywhere that a class holds stored records. Every class below is one this SDK reads and writes as a record and that rule does not reach, so without this file the derived table would silently omit it -- and an omitted record type looks exactly like a class that does not exist.
$established: 2026-09-02. Filed as jayostis/spec#50, which asks for one rdfs:subClassOf axiom per class. This is the same defect jayostis/spec#13 fixed for seven other classes, where it was described as invisible in both directions -- the gate could not see them, and they could not be baselined either, because the baseline is the gate's output. Delete an entry the moment spec declares the axiom; the derivation test is what says when.
